surface.opening_scene: First-person: Nia leading a 'resonance session' with her team - four minds connected through shared neural interfaces, their combined emotional states feeding a generative system that none of them fully controls.

visible_elements.name: The Conductor
visible_elements.description: Artist who pioneered 'collective resonance' - multi-brain creative sessions where team members share neural states. Leads but doesn't dominate; more facilitator than sole creator.

visible_elements.name: The Skeptic
visible_elements.description: Team member who joined from traditional art background. Talented but uncomfortable with the dissolution of individual authorship. Represents internal tension.

visible_elements.name: The Critic
visible_elements.description: Art writer who's documented Nia's rise. Intellectually supportive but personally troubled by what collective creation means for the idea of artistic genius.

visible_elements.name: The Resonance Chamber
visible_elements.description: Circular room designed for collective sessions. Five stations arranged facing center, where the shared visualization emerges. Acoustic dampening, controlled lighting.

visible_elements.name: Collective Neural Interface
visible_elements.description: System that reads multiple people's emotional states and combines them into unified input for generative models. Not telepathy - emotional resonance.

foundation.core_premise: By 2035, multi-brain interfaces allow small groups to share emotional states during creative sessions - not reading thoughts, but feeling each other's feelings. Nia pioneered 'collective resonance' art: works created by teams whose combined emotional signatures feed generative AI. The art that emerges belongs to no single person. This challenges everything about artistic identity, authorship, and the myth of individual genius.

rules.statement: Collective interfaces share emotional states, not thoughts. You feel what others feel, but don't know why they feel it. Intimacy without transparency.
Group emotional dynamics are emergent - the combined state is not simply averaged, but something new that depends on relationships and group chemistry.
Sessions require 'tuning' - groups need practice together before their combined signal becomes coherent. Like a band learning to play together.
Credit and ownership in collective art is legally and philosophically unresolved. Some collectives share equally; some have 'leads' who take primary credit; disputes are common.

systems.name: Collective Neural Interface
systems.how_it_works: Multiple EEG headsets feed into shared processing system. Emotional states are extracted and combined using learned fusion model. Combined emotional vector feeds generative AI. Optional: participants can 'feel' the group's combined state through subtle haptic feedback.
systems.limitations: Groups larger than 5-6 become incoherent. Requires extensive calibration as group. Emotionally exhausting - sessions limited to 2-3 hours. Some personality types don't integrate well.

systems.name: Resonance Visualization
systems.how_it_works: Real-time display showing each participant's emotional contribution and the emergent group state. Helps participants understand the collective dynamics during sessions.
systems.limitations: Visualization is interpretive, not precise. Can create self-consciousness that disrupts natural emotional flow.
